# Duplicate @property decorator on monday method breaks weekly scheduling

When trying to schedule a job to run on Monday using the `.monday` property, I'm getting a TypeError. This seems to be caused by having two `@property` decorators on the `monday` method.

## Reproduction

```python
from schedule import every

# This fails with TypeError: 'property' object is not callable
every().monday.do(lambda: print("This should run on Monday"))
```

The error occurs when trying to use any of the weekday properties (monday, tuesday, etc.) for scheduling. The code is trying to access the property as a method, but due to the duplicate decorator, it's not working correctly.

## Expected behavior

The `.monday` property should allow scheduling a job to run on Monday, as it did before. The same applies to other weekday properties.

## Actual behavior

Trying to use `.monday` or other weekday properties results in a TypeError: 'property' object is not callable.

This issue affects all weekly scheduling that uses specific weekdays, breaking a core functionality of the library.
